title: Why principles: the universal foundation of the method
blurb: Explain why the seven principles are obligations, why all seven must be applied, and why tailoring cannot remove them.
question: A project team uses every PRINCE2 template but has decided to skip stage boundaries to save time. Is it still a PRINCE2 project?

teach.body: PRINCE2 rests on seven principles: guiding obligations and good practices that decide whether a project is genuinely being managed with PRINCE2. Apply all seven and it is a PRINCE2 project. Leave even one out and it is not, however many PRINCE2 documents it produces. In plain English: the principles are the non-negotiable rules; everything else is how you play.

teach.body: PRINCE2 is used for very different projects, so it does not dictate exactly how to fit the method to each one. Instead it gives guidance through its principles. That is why two projects in the same organization can look quite different on the surface (different documents, reporting cycles, team set-ups) yet both be fully PRINCE2: each applies the same seven principles in a way that suits it.

teach.caption: Tailoring changes HOW the method is applied. It never decides WHETHER a principle applies.

teach.h: Worked scenario: one organization, two very different projects
teach.body: At Westmoor Housing Trust, project manager Priya Okafor runs two projects. A small office move merges its brief and business case into one short document and sends highlight reports by email. A larger tenant portal has formal stage reviews and a separate quality review plan. Both have a justified business case, a lessons log, a board with business, user and supplier interests, stages, tolerances and product descriptions. Both are PRINCE2: the principles are identical; only their application differs.

rows.label: Merging the brief and business case on a small project
Calling work packages 'job cards' to match company language
Removing stage boundaries so delivery runs straight through
Starting work with no reason recorded for doing the project

teach.note: If a change removes the obligation itself, it is not tailoring.

teach.text: Classic trap: 'we tailored out manage by stages because the project is small'. Principles cannot be tailored away. A small project may have just two stages (initiation plus one delivery stage), but it still has stages. And remember that tailoring is itself one of the seven principles.

items: Principles are guiding obligations and good practices: the foundation of the five integrated elements.
All seven must be applied for a project to be a PRINCE2 project.
PRINCE2 guides through principles rather than prescribing one way, so application differs between projects.
Processes, practices, roles, products and terminology can be tailored; the principles cannot.

summary: You can now explain why the seven principles are the foundation of PRINCE2 and why every one of them must be applied. You can also tell the difference between tailoring how the method is applied and wrongly dropping a principle.

A.q: Which statement best describes the PRINCE2 principles?
options: Optional good practices chosen to suit each project
Guiding obligations and good practices behind the method
Detailed procedures that describe each process activity
Aspects of project management addressed continually
A.why: The principles are guiding obligations and good practices; they decide whether a project is genuinely managed with PRINCE2 (manual 1.2, ch 2).

whyNot.0: They are obligations, not options: all seven must be applied.
whyNot.2: Activity-level procedures belong to the processes, which list recommended activities.
whyNot.3: Aspects of project management addressed throughout the lifecycle describes the practices.

A.q: A project follows the PRINCE2 processes and uses its templates but has removed all stage boundaries. Which statement is correct?
options: It is a PRINCE2 project because it uses the processes
It is a PRINCE2 project because tailoring allows this
It is not a PRINCE2 project because a principle is missing
It is not a PRINCE2 project because it needs three stages
A.why: All seven principles must be applied. With no stages, manage by stages is not applied, so the project is not a PRINCE2 project.

whyNot.0: Using processes and templates does not make a project PRINCE2 if a principle is not applied.
whyNot.1: Tailoring adapts how the method is applied; it cannot remove a principle.
whyNot.3: The minimum is two stages (initiation plus at least one delivery stage), not three.

A.q: Why does PRINCE2 give guidance through principles instead of prescribing exactly how to fit the method to each project?
options: So that every project in an organization is run identically
So that project boards can choose which principles to adopt
So that specialist techniques are defined for each industry
So that the method can be applied to suit each project
A.why: Because PRINCE2 is used for a wide range of projects, it guides through principles; the method can then be applied differently on each project, even within one organization.

whyNot.0: The point is the opposite: projects in one organization may apply the method differently.
whyNot.1: Boards cannot choose to drop principles; all seven apply.
whyNot.2: PRINCE2 is not specific to any industry and does not define specialist techniques.

B.q: Identify the missing word in the following sentence. The [?] are the foundation of PRINCE2: if they are not all applied, the project is not a PRINCE2 project.
options: practices
processes
principles
management approaches
B.why: The principles are the foundation element; applying all seven is what makes a project a PRINCE2 project.

whyNot.0: Practices are aspects of project management applied throughout, built on the principles.
whyNot.1: Processes describe the lifecycle activities; they are built on the principles.
whyNot.3: Management approaches are management products created in initiation, not the foundation of the method.

B.q: Which of the five integrated elements decides whether a project is genuinely being managed using PRINCE2?
options: Principles
People
Project context
Practices
B.why: The principles decide whether a project is genuinely PRINCE2: if they are not applied, it is not a PRINCE2 project (manual 1.2).

whyNot.1: People are at the centre of the method, but they do not define whether it is PRINCE2.
whyNot.2: Project context shapes how the method is applied, not whether it is PRINCE2.
whyNot.3: Practices must be applied, but the defining test is the seven principles.

B.q:
Which two statements about the principles are correct?
1. All seven principles must be applied for a project to be a PRINCE2 project.
2. A project board may agree to drop a principle on a small project.
3. Two projects in the same organization may apply PRINCE2 differently.
4. The principles prescribe the exact format of each management product.
options: 1 and 2
1 and 3
2 and 4
3 and 4
B.why: Statement 1 is the defining rule. Statement 3 follows from guidance through principles: the method is applied to suit each project.

whyNot.0: Statement 2 is false: principles cannot be tailored away, even on a small project.
whyNot.2: Both are false: principles are not dropped, and product formats can be tailored.
whyNot.3: Statement 4 is false: management products can be merged, renamed or reformatted.

C.q: A small project merges its project brief and business case and renames work packages to match company terms. It applies all seven principles. Which statement is correct?
options: It has dropped a principle and is no longer PRINCE2
It is tailoring the method and remains a PRINCE2 project
It is tailoring the principles to suit its smaller size
It needs business layer approval to remain PRINCE2
C.why: Merging documents and changing terminology are tailoring of products and terms. With all seven principles applied, it remains PRINCE2.

whyNot.0: No principle has been removed; only products and terms have changed.
whyNot.2: The principles are not tailored; the method (products, terms) is.
whyNot.3: Tailoring is agreed and documented within the project; it does not decide whether the project is PRINCE2.

C.q: Which of these can NOT be tailored on a PRINCE2 project?
options: The terminology used in the project
The format of the management products
The principles applied to the project
The way processes are combined
C.why: Processes, practices, roles, management products and terminology can be tailored. The principles cannot.

whyNot.0: Terminology can be tailored to match the organization's own terms.
whyNot.1: Management products can be merged, split, renamed or given different formats.
whyNot.3: Processes can be combined, simplified or done in more detail.

C.q: How do the principles relate to the other integrated elements of PRINCE2?
options: They replace the processes on smaller, simpler projects
They form a subset of practices applied during initiation
They describe the lifecycle from pre-project to closure
They are the foundation that the other elements build on
C.why: Figure 1.1 shows the principles as the foundation, with people, practices and processes built on them inside the project context.

whyNot.0: Principles do not replace processes; all elements are applied, tailored to suit the project.
whyNot.1: Principles are a separate element and apply throughout, not just in initiation.
whyNot.2: Describing the lifecycle from pre-project to closure is the role of the processes.

reteach.title: Rules of the game versus how you play it
reteach.question: Picture a sport played at a local park and in a stadium. Pitch size and kit differ, but some rules never change. Which parts of PRINCE2 are the rules?

blocks.h: The rules stay; the setting changes
blocks.body: A park game and a stadium final look very different, yet both are the same sport because the core rules hold. PRINCE2 works the same way. The seven principles are the rules: they hold on every PRINCE2 project. Processes, practices, documents, roles and terms are like the pitch and kit: they can be adapted to the project's size, risk and setting.

blocks.text: A project that applies six principles out of seven is not 'mostly PRINCE2'. It is not a PRINCE2 project.

explain.body: The principles are guiding obligations and good practices. Applying all seven is what makes a project a PRINCE2 project; using the templates is not enough.

test.q: A project applies six of the seven principles. What is its status?
options: It is a PRINCE2 project with tailoring
It is not considered a PRINCE2 project
It is PRINCE2 once the board approves it
It is PRINCE2 for its delivery stages
test.why: All seven principles must be applied; without one of them, the project is not a PRINCE2 project.

whyNot.0: Tailoring cannot remove a principle, so this is not tailoring.
whyNot.2: Board approval of tailoring cannot restore a missing principle.
whyNot.3: The principles apply across the whole project, not stage by stage.

explain.body: PRINCE2 does not prescribe one way of fitting the method to a project. It guides through principles, so the same organization can apply the method quite differently on different projects.

test.q: Two projects in one council apply PRINCE2 in very different ways. What best explains this?
options: One of the two projects must be leaving out a principle
The council has written its own method for each project
The principles guide a method tailored to each project
The processes are optional on the smaller of the projects
test.why: Because PRINCE2 guides through principles, the method is applied differently to suit each project, even within one organization.

whyNot.0: Difference in application does not mean a principle is missing.
whyNot.1: Each project uses PRINCE2, tailored; no separate method is needed.
whyNot.3: Processes can be tailored, for example combined, but are still applied.

explain.body: Of the five integrated elements (principles, people, practices, processes, project context), the principles sit at the base. Everything else is built on them.

test.q: In the five integrated elements of PRINCE2 7, which element is the foundation?
options: Principles
People
Processes
Project context
test.why: Figure 1.1 places the principles as the foundation, with practices, people and processes built on them.

whyNot.1: People are at the centre of the method, not its foundation.
whyNot.2: Processes are built on the principles.
whyNot.3: Project context surrounds the other elements rather than forming the base.

explain.h: Tailor the method, keep the principles
explain.body: Processes, practices, roles, products and terminology can be tailored. The principles cannot. A change that removes the obligation itself is not tailoring.

test.q: Which change would stop a project being a PRINCE2 project?
options: Using the organization's own terminology
Producing highlight reports by email
Adding an agile coach to the team
Removing the reviews between stages
test.why: Without review and decision points between stages, manage by stages is not applied, so a principle is missing.

whyNot.0: Using the organization's terms is a recognized form of tailoring.
whyNot.1: Changing the format of reports is tailoring.
whyNot.2: Adding a role, such as an agile coach, is tailoring of roles.
